nodes.name: Optimized NiFeMo/NF electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Ternary NiFeMo/NF ultra-thin sheets were synthesized via electrodeposition on nickel foam with optimized atomic ratio of raw material feed Ni:Fe:Mo = 9:2:1. Different Mo/Fe ratios were tested and Ni:Fe:Mo = 9:2:1 showed best performance (Fig. S7†).
nodes.source_text: we synthesized Mo doped NiFe (oxy)hydroxide (NiFeMo/NF) ... via an electrodeposition approach... When the molar ratio of the raw material feed during the synthesis of NiFeMo/NF is Ni:Fe:Mo = 9:2:1, the best electrocatalytic activity for the OER is obtained.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe displays uniform nanosheet arrays vertically grown on Ni foam; NiFeMo exhibits porous stacked lamellar layer covering Ni foam surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1a–e, the SEM image of NiFe displays a structure of uniform nanosheet arrays vertically grown on the open porous skeleton of Ni foam, while the NiFeMo sample exhibits a porous stacked lamellar layer covering the surface of Ni foam.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe and NiFeMo show ultra-thin nanosheet morphologies favorable for charge transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM images (Fig. 1b and f) further confirmed the ultra-thin nanosheet morphologies of the NiFe and NiFeMo electrocatalysts, and this morphology is favorable for charge transfer.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe shows lattice fringes of 2.68 Å (012 plane of NiFe LDH) and 2.40 Å (101 plane of NiOOH); NiFeMo shows 2.42 Å and ~3.48 Å corresponding to (101) and (006) planes of NiOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Clear lattice fringes with interplanar spacings of 2.68 and 2.40 Å can be indexed to the (012) plane of NiFe LDH and the (101) plane of NiOOH, respectively. The interplanar spacing of the crystalline phase in the NiFeMo/NF catalyst is 2.42 and ~3.48 Å, which corresponds to the (101) and (006) crystal planes of NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni, Fe, O uniformly distributed in NiFe; Ni, Fe, O, Mo uniformly distributed in NiFeMo confirming successful Mo incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the NiFe catalyst (Fig. 1d), the Ni, Fe, and O elements are uniformly distributed in the NiFe nanosheet structure. In addition to the uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, and O elements, the Mo element is also evenly distributed in NiFeMo.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe shows Ni2+ (854.9, 872.4 eV) and Ni3+ (855.8, 873.6 eV); NiFeMo shows decreased Ni3+/Ni2+ ratio, Fe 2p shifts to lower binding energies (712.1, 725.9 eV from 712.4, 726.1 eV), Mo3d at 232.4, 235.5 eV indicates Mo6+.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Ni 2p XPS spectra of NiFe (oxy)hydroxide exhibits Ni 2p3/2 and Ni 2p1/2 peaks along with satellite peaks (Fig. 2a). The deconvolution results of the Ni 2p peak demonstrate the co-existence of Ni3+ (855.8 and 873.6 eV) and Ni2+ (854.9 and 872.4 eV). Incorporating Mo leads to a decreased ratio of Ni3+ in NiFeMo (oxy)hydroxide.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl of NiFeMo/NF is 7.0 mF cm-2 and NiFe/NF is 5.95 mF cm-2; corresponding ECSA of 175 cm2ESCA and 149 cm2ESCA respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By plotting the current density against the scan rate, the Cdl of NiFeMo and NiFe-LDH was determined to be 7.0 and 5.95 mF cm-2, respectively. Assuming that the specific capacitance of the ideal plane is 0.04 mF cm-2, the ESCAs of NiFe/NF and NiFeMo/NF are 149 cmESCA2 and 175 cmESCA2, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe shows β-NiOOH (475, 557 cm-1, I557/I475=1.12) transforming to γ-NiOOH at 0.5 V vs Ag (I551/I468=0.82); NiFeMo transformation shifts to higher potential of 0.6 V vs Ag.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At the open circuit potential, two peaks corresponding to β-NiOOH at ~475 and 557 cm-1 with an I557/I475 intensity ratio of 1.12 were observed... Once the applied potential reaches 0.5 V and increases further, the intensity ratio of the peaks at 468 cm-1 and 551 cm-1 I551/I468 reduced to 0.82, which can be assigned to the transformation of β-NiOOH into the γ-NiOOH phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: Charge-transfer resistances: NiFeMo/NF 0.61 Ω, NiFe/NF 1.95 Ω, NiMo/NF 2.04 Ω, Ni/NF 22.5 Ω.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The radius of the fitted semicircle indicates that the charge-transfer resistances of NiFeMo/NF, NiFe/NF, NiMo/NF and Ni/NF at the electrode/electrolyte interface are 0.61, 1.95, 2.04 and 22.5 Ω, respectively.
